   142	
   143	Workflow source is authoritative for this intended graph and its permission
   144	edges. A hosted GitHub readback is required to prove the actor, SHA, jobs,
   145	environment, conclusion, and retained artifact for one execution.
   146	
   147	All credentialed Alchemy workflows select the repository-owned
   148	`site-ci-env-v1` profile. On a fresh CI runner the installed Alchemy beta.64
   149	configures that profile with `method: env`. A pinned Doppler fetch action reads
   150	the protected job Environment's read-only `DOPPLER_TOKEN` and maps the required
   151	provider outputs into the exact provider step. This prevents a persistent
   152	self-hosted runner's unrelated `default` OAuth profile from taking precedence
   153	over the job credentials. The profile name is non-secret; credentials remain
   154	confined to each protected workflow step and are not written into source or
   155	receipts.
   156	
   157	## Artifact and build boundary
   158	
   159	Each hosted job receives a fresh filesystem. The granular quality graph
   160	uploads the exact candidate's built workspace outputs for later quality and
   161	branch-preview jobs in the same workflow run. The browser and branch-preview
   162	jobs download those named artifacts after the source receipt has been accepted;
   163	GitHub's artifact service verifies the transferred archive, and the workflow
   164	contract also requires the non-empty upload digests emitted by the accepted
   165	build job. This handoff avoids rebuilding the quality graph and makes the
   166	generated-asset check operate on the accepted build output. It is not a
   167	provider-deployment identity.
   168	
   169	Production and fixed proof therefore still build the app's workspace
   170	dependencies before
   171	Alchemy invokes the Vite/TanStack Start build. Repository checks and the later
   172	Alchemy build are related to the same commit, but they are not automatically
   173	the same byte artifact. HGI-106's two-copy beta.63 tracer found identical
   174	static-asset hashes but different server-bundle hashes because absolute
   175	checkout paths entered the generated TanStack manifest and Distilled worker
   176	entry. The supported claim is `same-source-rebuild-only`, not exact artifact
   177	promotion.
   178	
   179	Site retains `Cloudflare.Website.Vite`. Its installed implementation runs Vite
   180	during Worker resource preparation. Although the lower-level Worker API can
   181	upload an already-complete runtime-ready ESM bundle with `bundle: false`,
   182	Alchemy does not expose Website.Vite's collected TanStack output as a public
   183	first-class prebuilt artifact handoff. Adopting private collector internals
   184	would move routing, asset, Worker-first, cache, ownership, and rollback risk
   185	into this repository without establishing byte identity.
   186	
   187	The production command emits the exact candidate SHA, installed Alchemy
   188	version, a digest of the named source/config owners, Alchemy's assets, bundle,
   189	input, and metadata hashes, and Worker identity. After deployment it performs
   190	a read-only Cloudflare deployments API readback for that Worker and emits the
   191	latest fully promoted deployment and version identities. Missing, split, or
   192	mismatched readback fails closed. The HGI-107 packet contract retains that
   193	output; HGI-112 must qualify and prove the live provider/API boundary before
   194	generic AOX/HGI-112 packet claims are accepted. Literal MCP-006 uses its
   195	separately admitted provider/public receipt and does not claim HGI-112 settings
   196	or packet proof.
   197	
   198	The quality graph's `bun run build` includes the app-owned
   199	`asset-build-proof` gate. It checks generated server and client CSS references
   200	against the emitted `dist/client` files before a candidate can be accepted and
   201	emits one Schema-owned `accepted` or `rejected` receipt from a typed Effect
   202	program. That local receipt proves only generated output; it is not public or
   203	provider evidence.
   204	After Alchemy applies its own same-source build, the production route verifier
   205	must also fetch the exact hashed assets referenced by `/` and
   206	`/posts/hello-world`; a `404`, empty body, or HTML fallback is a failed
   207	deployment even when the Worker is reachable and provider metadata reports an
   208	asset binding.
   209	
   210	Vite entrypoints are host adapters. Durable build detection and virtual-module
   211	policy belong in [`apps/web/src/lib/build/vite`](../../apps/web/src/lib/build/vite/);
   212	the shared build-time observability plan belongs in
   213	[`apps/web/src/lib/build/observability`](../../apps/web/src/lib/build/observability/);
   214	and Website options, deployment outputs, qualification, authority, and the
   215	site-proof manifest belong in their capability-owned subdirectories under
   216	[`apps/web/src/lib/build`](../../apps/web/src/lib/build/) with focused tests.
   217	Application packages expose built default exports for production resolution
   218	and source exports only under the repository's development source condition.
   219	
   220	The provider-neutral app graph resolves the observability deployment adapter
   221	to an absent runtime-config service, so local Vite and ordinary client builds
   222	neither import a Cloudflare binding nor initialize an OTLP exporter. An Alchemy
   223	Website build aliases only that deployment adapter to the Cloudflare
   224	implementation. The
   225	Cloudflare adapter imports `env` from `cloudflare:workers`, reads the optional
   226	`SITE_AXIOM_METRICS_CONFIG` Secrets Store binding asynchronously, and provides
   227	the metrics-only server Layer. Vite preserves `cloudflare:workers` as one exact
   228	Alchemy-build external because it is supplied by the Worker runtime, not an npm
   229	module. The root Alchemy stack is the sole owner that declares that binding,
   230	and only for `site-proof` and `prod`.
   231	
   232	## Identity and capability boundaries
   233	
   234	Quality, fixed proof, production, and release have distinct capabilities.
   235	Workflow YAML must request only the repository permissions and environment
   236	secrets its job needs; it must not inherit a wider secret set. Every external
   237	action is pinned to a full commit SHA. Repository commands run with the Bun
   238	version selected by the checked-in version owners.
   239	
   240	The exact-main caller passes no provider secrets and uses no broad inheritance.
   241	The `site-proof` Environment token reads only `site/stg`; the Production token
   242	reads only `site/prd`. The pinned fetch action exposes named outputs and the
   243	workflow maps those outputs only to the provider steps that need them. Quality
   244	and release receive neither provider set.
   245	
   246	The `cloudflare-branch-preview.yml` reusable workflow is a deliberately narrow
   247	provider exception for the trusted initial allowlist. The sole PR orchestrator
   248	passes the candidate SHA, quality-accepted SHA, PR number, and both build and
   249	source-receipt artifact digests from one workflow run. The reusable job rejects
   250	a mismatched SHA or missing digest, downloads and verifies the exact source
   251	receipt and handed-off output, then re-reads the live PR before provider
   252	mutation. It accepts only the exact head SHA of a same-repository `crcorbett`
   253	pull request, requires the externally
   254	read-back repository configuration variable
   255	`SITE_BRANCH_PREVIEW_ENABLED=true` and the `preview` Environment, and exposes only
   256	the `site/stg_preview` Doppler outputs `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and
   257	`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` on the single deploy step. Its Alchemy stage is
   258	`pr-{number}` and the stack's
   259	non-production branch declares only `Website`: no Axiom provider, Secrets
   260	Store secret, production route, or fixed `site-proof` resource is reachable

    12	## Preconditions and authority
    13	
    14	This runbook applies only to the Pollsor repository's CI cache and workflow
    15	controls. It does not configure a Vercel deployment or application runtime.

    18	workflow files, the GitHub repository settings, and the Personal Vercel team
    19	settings read back at the time of the operation. Dated receipts are evidence,
    20	not durable provider state.

    25	- the exact GitHub repository and `main` branch;

    27	  token, or set the `TURBO_TEAM` variable;
    28	- the target environment and duration;

    73	## Procedure and bounded evidence
    74	
    75	### 1. Inspect the candidate
    76	
    77	From the Pollsor checkout, confirm the target revision and that unrelated work
    78	is preserved:

    81	git status --short --branch
    82	git rev-parse HEAD
    83	bun pm cache
    84	bun run docs:check
    85	bun run verification
    86	```
    87	
    88	Each command is owned by the repository maintainer. The expected postcondition
    89	is a clean or explicitly accounted-for checkout, a reported Bun package-cache
    90	path, passing current documentation checks, and a passing repository gate. A
    91	failed command stops the operation and keeps the exact failure receipt; it is
    92	not repaired by weakening the workflow or cache policy.

   175	## Rollback, escalation, and cleanup
   176	
   177	The last known-good state is the prior workflow revision with the same
   178	repository checks and no Remote Cache controls. To roll back:
   179	
   180	1. disable or remove the `TURBO_TEAM`/`TURBO_TOKEN` controls from the approved
   181	   GitHub target, or disable the team's Remote Caching through the approved
   182	   provider procedure;
   183	2. restore the prior workflow/Turbo configuration as one repository slice;
   184	3. revoke or rotate the exact CI token if exposure, scope error, or unexplained
   185	   cache behaviour occurred; and
   186	4. rerun `bun run verification` and retain the failed/blocked receipt.
   187	
   188	Escalate to the Pollsor CI maintainer for workflow failures, to the Personal
   189	Vercel owner for team/token/cache readback, and to the GitHub repository owner
   190	for secret visibility or fork-event behaviour. Stop on secret exposure,
   191	unexpected cache contents, a missing output, a provider/team mismatch, or a
   192	workflow that would execute untrusted code with a write token.
   193	
   194	Cleanup includes removing temporary local cache diagnostics and ensuring no
   195	token, browser state, provider response containing secrets, or candidate
   196	artifact remains in the repository or uploaded artifact. The runbook does not
   197	claim that disabling Remote Cache rolls back a Vercel deployment, removes old
   198	cache entries, or changes already-completed hosted jobs.
   199	
   200	After the repository change is merged and a fresh `main` workflow proves the
   201	Doppler path, a separate authorised cleanup may remove the old repository
   202	secret `TURBO_TOKEN` and variable `TURBO_TEAM`, then revoke only the superseded
   203	Vercel token. Record the exact deleted names and revocation metadata without
   204	values. This pull request must retain them so current `main` cannot break before
   205	the new workflow exists.

   208	
   209	Local verification proves repository source and configuration only. A workflow
   210	run proves the named CI jobs for its revision and runner. Only a separate
   211	provider readback proves Remote Cache team configuration; only matched cold and
   212	warm hosted runs support a performance comparison. Neither CI nor this runbook
   213	proves Preview, Production, deployment, provider model behaviour, Microsoft,
   214	or user-facing Pollsor operation.

   175	## Rollback, escalation, and cleanup
   176	
   177	The last known-good state is the prior workflow revision with the same
   178	repository checks and no Remote Cache controls. To roll back:
   179	
   180	1. disable or remove the `TURBO_TEAM`/`TURBO_TOKEN` controls from the approved
   181	   GitHub target, or disable the team's Remote Caching through the approved
   182	   provider procedure;
   183	2. restore the prior workflow/Turbo configuration as one repository slice;
   184	3. revoke or rotate the exact CI token if exposure, scope error, or unexplained
   185	   cache behaviour occurred; and
   186	4. rerun `bun run verification` and retain the failed/blocked receipt.
   187	
   188	Escalate to the Pollsor CI maintainer for workflow failures, to the Personal
   189	Vercel owner for team/token/cache readback, and to the GitHub repository owner
   190	for secret visibility or fork-event behaviour. Stop on secret exposure,
   191	unexpected cache contents, a missing output, a provider/team mismatch, or a
   192	workflow that would execute untrusted code with a write token.
   193	
   194	Cleanup includes removing temporary local cache diagnostics and ensuring no
   195	token, browser state, provider response containing secrets, or candidate
   196	artifact remains in the repository or uploaded artifact. The runbook does not
   197	claim that disabling Remote Cache rolls back a Vercel deployment, removes old
   198	cache entries, or changes already-completed hosted jobs.

   200	After the repository change is merged and a fresh `main` workflow proves the
   201	Doppler path, a separate authorised cleanup may remove the old repository
   202	secret `TURBO_TOKEN` and variable `TURBO_TEAM`, then revoke only the superseded
   203	Vercel token. Record the exact deleted names and revocation metadata without
   204	values. This pull request must retain them so current `main` cannot break before
   205	the new workflow exists.

   208	
   209	Local verification proves repository source and configuration only. A workflow
   210	run proves the named CI jobs for its revision and runner. Only a separate
   211	provider readback proves Remote Cache team configuration; only matched cold and
   212	warm hosted runs support a performance comparison. Neither CI nor this runbook
   213	proves Preview, Production, deployment, provider model behaviour, Microsoft,

    15	controls. It does not configure a Vercel deployment or application runtime.

    34	confirm that the Cooper Chrome profile is selected before reading the target.

    39	separate approval receipt for the exact Vercel team and GitHub secret/variable
    40	resources. A missing team identity, token scope, GitHub visibility rule, or

    73	## Procedure and bounded evidence
    74	
    75	### 1. Inspect the candidate
    76	
    77	From the Pollsor checkout, confirm the target revision and that unrelated work
    78	is preserved:
    79	
    80	```bash
    81	git status --short --branch
    82	git rev-parse HEAD
    83	bun pm cache
    84	bun run docs:check
    85	bun run verification
    86	```
    87	
    88	Each command is owned by the repository maintainer. The expected postcondition
    89	is a clean or explicitly accounted-for checkout, a reported Bun package-cache
    90	path, passing current documentation checks, and a passing repository gate. A
    91	failed command stops the operation and keeps the exact failure receipt; it is
    92	not repaired by weakening the workflow or cache policy.
    93	
    94	### 2. Read back provider and GitHub controls
    95	
    96	Using the approved Personal Vercel interface, read back the exact team,
    97	Remote Caching enablement, token scope, token expiry/rotation metadata, and
    98	the team member/principal identity. Do not print or retain the token value.

   107	Using the Personal Doppler workplace, read back only the workplace plan,
   108	project/config names, secret key names, service-token access, scope and expiry.
   109	Never read or record secret values. The Developer plan does not support the
   110	service-account identity required for Doppler OIDC, so this repository uses the
   111	documented config-scoped service-token fallback until the plan changes.

   113	Confirm that fork pull requests do not receive the write token. Confirm that
   114	the workflow's `pull_request` event is not a privileged candidate-checkout
   115	path. Record only names, scopes/classes, timestamps, and postconditions in the
   116	sanitised receipt.

   119	
   120	If the authority receipt permits the operation, create or rotate the expiring
   121	Personal Vercel token for the exact Remote Cache team. Stream its value directly
   122	into `TURBO_TOKEN` in Doppler project `pollsor`, config `ci`, without placing it
   123	in shell arguments, files, logs or receipts. Put `TURBO_TEAM` in the same config.
   124	Create a read-only, config-scoped, expiring Doppler service token and stream it
   125	directly into the GitHub `CI` Environment secret `DOPPLER_TOKEN`.
   126	
   127	The 2026-08-22 migration uses two 365-day credentials. Vercel token
   128	`pollsor-turbo-doppler-ci-2026-08-21` and Doppler service token
   129	`pollsor-github-ci-2026-08-22` both expire on 2027-08-22. Review and rotate
   130	them before that date. The names, access class and expiry are safe metadata;
   131	their values must never enter this repository or its evidence.
   132	
   133	The checked-in workflow uses
   134	`dopplerhq/secrets-fetch-action@451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534`
   135	(`v2.0.0`). Only the type, test and build jobs may reference the `CI`
   136	Environment. Each trusted job maps only `TURBO_TEAM` and `TURBO_TOKEN` outputs
   137	into its exact `*:internal` command. A fork job must take a separate step that
   138	does not run the Doppler action. Simulator and Eve jobs remain credential-free.
   139	The checked-in `apps/web/vercel.json` and `apps/agent/vercel.json` files also
   140	call `build:internal` with their exact app filter. Vercel builds must not call
   141	the person-facing Doppler wrapper or receive this GitHub CI credential set.
   142	
   143	Do not create a Vercel project, deployment, alias, domain, application
   144	environment variable, billing change, or unrelated token. Do not put a token
   145	in a workflow file. Do not run candidate code with a privileged secret on a
   146	fork event. Do not remove the old GitHub `TURBO_TOKEN` or `TURBO_TEAM`, or revoke
   147	the old Vercel token, before the replacement has passed on merged `main`.
   148	
   149	### 4. Verify with bounded runs
   150	
   151	Run one trusted same-repository PR or `main` workflow and record:
   152	
   153	- exact revision and workflow URL;
   154	- runner, Bun, Turbo, and action identities;
   155	- Bun cache restore/save result;
   156	- Turbo local/remote hit, miss, forced, skipped, and failure summary;
   157	- job durations and final summary result; and
   158	- absence of secret values from logs and artifacts.
   159	
   160	Read back Doppler project/config names, the exact two config key names, service
   161	token read-only access and expiry, and the GitHub `CI` Environment secret name.
   162	Do not use a successful fetch or green CI run as Vercel deployment proof.
   163	
   164	Run a fork/secret-withheld path or an approved provider read-only path. It must
   165	complete the same required checks, report that write credentials were withheld,
   166	and never present a write token to candidate code. A passing fork run is proof
   167	of the safety boundary and repository checks only; it is not proof of remote
   168	cache writes.
   169	
   170	The workflow's quality summary is the bounded artifact at
   171	`pollsor-ci-summary-<run-id>`. Keep the sanitised receipt under
   172	`docs/evidence/pollsor-ci-performance/`; do not copy mutable provider settings
   173	into this runbook.
   174	
   175	## Rollback, escalation, and cleanup
   176	
   177	The last known-good state is the prior workflow revision with the same
   178	repository checks and no Remote Cache controls. To roll back:
   179	
   180	1. disable or remove the `TURBO_TEAM`/`TURBO_TOKEN` controls from the approved
   181	   GitHub target, or disable the team's Remote Caching through the approved
   182	   provider procedure;
   183	2. restore the prior workflow/Turbo configuration as one repository slice;
   184	3. revoke or rotate the exact CI token if exposure, scope error, or unexplained
   185	   cache behaviour occurred; and
   186	4. rerun `bun run verification` and retain the failed/blocked receipt.
   187	
   188	Escalate to the Pollsor CI maintainer for workflow failures, to the Personal
   189	Vercel owner for team/token/cache readback, and to the GitHub repository owner
   190	for secret visibility or fork-event behaviour. Stop on secret exposure,
   191	unexpected cache contents, a missing output, a provider/team mismatch, or a
   192	workflow that would execute untrusted code with a write token.

   195	token, browser state, provider response containing secrets, or candidate

     1	# `@bundjil/infrastructure`
     2	
     3	Private repository infrastructure contracts and Alchemy providers for Bundjil.
     4	The package owns state-safe Schemas, branded identities, named services, safe
     5	errors, explicit live/memory Layers, adoption and inventory contracts, bounded
     6	receipts, and retained custom Resources.
     7	
     8	## Public exports
     9	
    10	- `@bundjil/infrastructure` — shared infrastructure contracts, services,
    11	  configuration, receipts, inventory, drift, state, adoption, and synthetic
    12	  provider capabilities.
    13	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/testing` — decoded deterministic test fixtures.
    14	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/vercel` — Vercel-owned Schemas, identities,
    15	  services, safe errors, and explicit read/write-capability Layers. Preview
    16	  configuration and stable-environment authority loaders expose only their
    17	  owner-named authority error and bounded reason Schema; raw Config,
    18	  filesystem, parser, and primitive-string failures remain private.
    19	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/photon` — retained Photon observation Resources and
    20	  the separately composed Preview webhook-binding capability.
    21	
    22	Raw provider clients, wire DTOs, credentials, secret values, and unchecked
    23	provider failures are not public exports.
    24	
    25	Infrastructure operator programs keep owner-local Schema tagged errors until
    26	their final process adapter. That adapter alone may render the stable bounded
    27	status/reason and set the documented exit code. Root lint rejects primitive
    28	`Effect.fail`, `Effect.failSync`, and `Effect.mapError` values across every
    29	script in `scripts/`. Reusable live Layers retain typed construction failures;
    30	commands provide their runtime inside the final catch/exit boundary, and root
    31	lint rejects `Layer.orDie` in package source and infrastructure scripts.
    32	Subprocess fixtures exercise deterministic foreground stops and missing Layer
    33	configuration without provider transport or raw Cause output. Mutating
    34	commands capture authority, configuration, runtime acquisition, foreground
    35	work, readback, and Schema receipt encoding in that boundary; expected failure
    36	must not fall through to a runtime stack reporter. The private automatic
    37	Production entrypoint follows the same process contract: it keeps the existing
    38	Schema-encoded deployment receipt on success and emits only
    39	`{"status":"blocked"}` with exit code `1` after any Config, Layer, deployment,
    40	rollback, health, or encoding failure. That bounded result is not a deployment
    41	or rollback diagnosis; GitHub logs and Vercel readback remain the operational
    42	evidence owners.
    43	
    44	## Supported commands
    45	
    46	Run package checks from the repository root:
    47	
    48	```sh
    49	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure check-types
    50	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure test
    51	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure build
    52	```
    53	
    54	Public repository command names are `infrastructure:inventory`,
    55	`infrastructure:adoption-manifest`, `infrastructure:adoption-proof`,
    56	`infrastructure:drift-report`, `infrastructure:preview-plan`,
    57	`infrastructure:preview-apply`, `infrastructure:preview-sync`,
    58	`infrastructure:preview-drift`, `infrastructure:preview-repair`,
    59	`infrastructure:preview-rollback-plan`, `infrastructure:preview-rollback`,
    60	`infrastructure:preview-state-migration`,
    61	`infrastructure:production-state-migration`,
    62	`infrastructure:stable-preview-plan`,
    63	`infrastructure:stable-preview-apply`,
    64	`infrastructure:stable-preview-sync`,
    65	`infrastructure:stable-production-plan`,
    66	`infrastructure:stable-production-apply`,
    67	`infrastructure:stable-production-sync`,
    68	`infrastructure:photon-candidate-inventory`,
    69	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-register`,
    70	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-binding`,
    71	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-register`,
    72	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-delete`, and
    73	`infrastructure:vercel-git-link-authority`. `production:deploy` is the private
    74	post-CI Production entrypoint. It is owned by the exact-SHA `Production`
    75	workflow, uses two separately revocable Vercel credentials project-scoped to
    76	the exact Personal projects and selected by exact project binding, proves the
    77	assigned-project read and sibling-project denial before custody, and stages both apps with
    78	domains skipped, validates immutable candidates, promotes only while the
    79	candidate is still `main`, verifies the stable targets and proxy health, and
    80	restores the exact prior deployments on every non-success Effect exit after
    81	promotion starts, including interruption and defect paths. It is not an
    82	operator convenience command.
    83	
    84	`infrastructure:drift-report` uses a distinct project-scoped credential Layer.
    85	Its environment file supplies
    86	`BUNDJIL_INFRASTRUCTURE_VERCEL_PROJECT_CREDENTIALS_JSON`, a Schema-decoded
    87	non-empty array of unique project-ID/token bindings. Each token is issued for
    88	one exact Personal Vercel project and must pass the assigned-project read and
    89	sibling-project denial checks before custody. The Vercel adapter selects a
    90	redacted token only after receiving a decoded branded project ID, and the
    91	Alchemy project provider observes exactly the manifest projects rather than
    92	listing a whole team. Broad `VERCEL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ACCESS_TOKEN` custody remains
    93	limited to the separate inventory/adoption/operator paths.
    94	
    95	Marketplace attachment reads use only each exact project's decoded
    96	environment `contentHint`. Project tokens cannot enumerate the account-wide
    97	storage list, so the adapter never calls it. The accepted manifest database ID
    98	is retained only after the observable integration, configuration, resource and
    99	project identities match; it is not a fresh database-ID readback.
   100	
   101	The accepted Preview manifest is Schema-encoded first, then held in the exact
   102	GitHub manifest secret as an in-memory gzip/base64 transport because the raw
   103	155-resource JSON exceeds GitHub's secret-size boundary. The hosted workflow
   104	materialises the original JSON into mode-`0600` custody before this command
   105	Schema-decodes it and compares it with the exact configured accepted digest;
   106	the transport is never a second manifest authority.
   107	Vercel deployment responses may also contain named custom targets. The live
   108	adapter decodes those provider values but admits only `preview`, `production`,
   109	or the provider's legacy `null` Preview target into Bundjil observations;
   110	custom targets such as `staging` are ignored and are never relabelled Preview.
   111	The drift report keeps returned deployment observations strict across every
   112	typed field. If Vercel no longer returns an accepted historical deployment,
   113	the report records unavailable history without claiming drift, deletion,
   114	retention or repair authority. An accepted write-only environment baseline is
   115	continuous only when present provider revision metadata is unchanged and the
   116	accepted manifest records `ObservedUnknown`; the value itself is never proved.
   117	If native sync cannot complete, the operator log may expose only the closed
   118	typed provider-read error name and reason alongside the safe phase. It never
   119	emits the error message, request, response, URL, headers, provider payload or
   120	credential.
   121	
   122	## Claim boundary
   123	
   124	Package checks prove repository contracts only. They do not establish current
   125	provider state or authorize credentials, state migration, provider writes,
   126	deployment, promotion, messaging, billing, Preview, or Production operations.
   127	Current evidence belongs to task-scoped receipts and external readback.
   128	The automatic command's local tests prove orchestration and fail-closed
   129	behavior only; a successful hosted `Production` run plus Vercel readback is
   130	required to prove automatic deployment.
   131	
   132	Operational preconditions, authority, sequencing, evidence, rollback, stop,
   133	and escalation rules are owned by the

     1	# `@bundjil/infrastructure`
     2	
     3	Private repository infrastructure contracts and Alchemy providers for Bundjil.
     4	The package owns state-safe Schemas, branded identities, named services, safe
     5	errors, explicit live/memory Layers, adoption and inventory contracts, bounded
     6	receipts, and retained custom Resources.
     7	
     8	## Public exports
     9	
    10	- `@bundjil/infrastructure` — shared infrastructure contracts, services,
    11	  configuration, receipts, inventory, drift, state, adoption, and synthetic
    12	  provider capabilities.
    13	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/testing` — decoded deterministic test fixtures.
    14	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/vercel` — Vercel-owned Schemas, identities,
    15	  services, safe errors, and explicit read/write-capability Layers. Preview
    16	  configuration and stable-environment authority loaders expose only their
    17	  owner-named authority error and bounded reason Schema; raw Config,
    18	  filesystem, parser, and primitive-string failures remain private.
    19	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/photon` — retained Photon observation Resources and
    20	  the separately composed Preview webhook-binding capability.
    21	
    22	Raw provider clients, wire DTOs, credentials, secret values, and unchecked
    23	provider failures are not public exports.
    24	
    25	Infrastructure operator programs keep owner-local Schema tagged errors until
    26	their final process adapter. That adapter alone may render the stable bounded
    27	status/reason and set the documented exit code. Root lint rejects primitive
    28	`Effect.fail`, `Effect.failSync`, and `Effect.mapError` values across every
    29	script in `scripts/`. Reusable live Layers retain typed construction failures;
    30	commands provide their runtime inside the final catch/exit boundary, and root
    31	lint rejects `Layer.orDie` in package source and infrastructure scripts.
    32	Subprocess fixtures exercise deterministic foreground stops and missing Layer
    33	configuration without provider transport or raw Cause output. Mutating
    34	commands capture authority, configuration, runtime acquisition, foreground
    35	work, readback, and Schema receipt encoding in that boundary; expected failure
    36	must not fall through to a runtime stack reporter. The private automatic
    37	Production entrypoint follows the same process contract: it keeps the existing
    38	Schema-encoded deployment receipt on success and emits only
    39	`{"status":"blocked"}` with exit code `1` after any Config, Layer, deployment,
    40	rollback, health, or encoding failure. That bounded result is not a deployment
    41	or rollback diagnosis; GitHub logs and Vercel readback remain the operational
    42	evidence owners.
    43	
    44	## Supported commands
    45	
    46	Run package checks from the repository root:
    47	
    48	```sh
    49	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure check-types
    50	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure test
    51	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure build
    52	```
    53	
    54	Public repository command names are `infrastructure:inventory`,
    55	`infrastructure:adoption-manifest`, `infrastructure:adoption-proof`,
    56	`infrastructure:drift-report`, `infrastructure:preview-plan`,
    57	`infrastructure:preview-apply`, `infrastructure:preview-sync`,
    58	`infrastructure:preview-drift`, `infrastructure:preview-repair`,
    59	`infrastructure:preview-rollback-plan`, `infrastructure:preview-rollback`,
    60	`infrastructure:preview-state-migration`,
    61	`infrastructure:production-state-migration`,
    62	`infrastructure:stable-preview-plan`,
    63	`infrastructure:stable-preview-apply`,
    64	`infrastructure:stable-preview-sync`,
    65	`infrastructure:stable-production-plan`,
    66	`infrastructure:stable-production-apply`,
    67	`infrastructure:stable-production-sync`,
    68	`infrastructure:photon-candidate-inventory`,
    69	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-register`,
    70	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-binding`,
    71	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-register`,
    72	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-delete`, and
    73	`infrastructure:vercel-git-link-authority`. `production:deploy` is the private
    74	post-CI Production entrypoint. It is owned by the exact-SHA `Production`
    75	workflow, uses two separately revocable Vercel credentials project-scoped to
    76	the exact Personal projects and selected by exact project binding, proves the
    77	assigned-project read and sibling-project denial before custody, and stages both apps with
    78	domains skipped, validates immutable candidates, promotes only while the
    79	candidate is still `main`, verifies the stable targets and proxy health, and
    80	restores the exact prior deployments on every non-success Effect exit after
    81	promotion starts, including interruption and defect paths. It is not an
    82	operator convenience command.
    83	
    84	`infrastructure:drift-report` uses a distinct project-scoped credential Layer.
    85	Its environment file supplies
    86	`BUNDJIL_INFRASTRUCTURE_VERCEL_PROJECT_CREDENTIALS_JSON`, a Schema-decoded
    87	non-empty array of unique project-ID/token bindings. Each token is issued for
    88	one exact Personal Vercel project and must pass the assigned-project read and
    89	sibling-project denial checks before custody. The Vercel adapter selects a
    90	redacted token only after receiving a decoded branded project ID, and the
    91	Alchemy project provider observes exactly the manifest projects rather than
    92	listing a whole team. Broad `VERCEL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ACCESS_TOKEN` custody remains
    93	limited to the separate inventory/adoption/operator paths.
    94	
    95	Marketplace attachment reads use only each exact project's decoded
    96	environment `contentHint`. Project tokens cannot enumerate the account-wide
    97	storage list, so the adapter never calls it. The accepted manifest database ID
    98	is retained only after the observable integration, configuration, resource and
    99	project identities match; it is not a fresh database-ID readback.
   100	
   101	The accepted Preview manifest is Schema-encoded first, then held in the exact
   102	GitHub manifest secret as an in-memory gzip/base64 transport because the raw
   103	155-resource JSON exceeds GitHub's secret-size boundary. The hosted workflow
   104	materialises the original JSON into mode-`0600` custody before this command
   105	Schema-decodes it and compares it with the exact configured accepted digest;
   106	the transport is never a second manifest authority.
   107	Vercel deployment responses may also contain named custom targets. The live
   108	adapter decodes those provider values but admits only `preview`, `production`,
   109	or the provider's legacy `null` Preview target into Bundjil observations;
   110	custom targets such as `staging` are ignored and are never relabelled Preview.
   111	The drift report keeps returned deployment observations strict across every
   112	typed field. If Vercel no longer returns an accepted historical deployment,
   113	the report records unavailable history without claiming drift, deletion,
   114	retention or repair authority. An accepted write-only environment baseline is
   115	continuous only when present provider revision metadata is unchanged and the
   116	accepted manifest records `ObservedUnknown`; the value itself is never proved.
   117	If native sync cannot complete, the operator log may expose only the closed
   118	typed provider-read error name and reason alongside the safe phase. It never
   119	emits the error message, request, response, URL, headers, provider payload or
   120	credential.
   121	
   122	## Claim boundary
   123	
   124	Package checks prove repository contracts only. They do not establish current
   125	provider state or authorize credentials, state migration, provider writes,
   126	deployment, promotion, messaging, billing, Preview, or Production operations.
   127	Current evidence belongs to task-scoped receipts and external readback.
   128	The automatic command's local tests prove orchestration and fail-closed
   129	behavior only; a successful hosted `Production` run plus Vercel readback is
   130	required to prove automatic deployment.
   131	
   132	Operational preconditions, authority, sequencing, evidence, rollback, stop,
   133	and escalation rules are owned by the
   134	[Alchemy infrastructure runbook](../../apps/agent/runbooks/alchemy-infrastructure.md).

     1	# `@bundjil/infrastructure`
     2	
     3	Private repository infrastructure contracts and Alchemy providers for Bundjil.
     4	The package owns state-safe Schemas, branded identities, named services, safe
     5	errors, explicit live/memory Layers, adoption and inventory contracts, bounded
     6	receipts, and retained custom Resources.
     7	
     8	## Public exports
     9	
    10	- `@bundjil/infrastructure` — shared infrastructure contracts, services,
    11	  configuration, receipts, inventory, drift, state, adoption, and synthetic
    12	  provider capabilities.
    13	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/testing` — decoded deterministic test fixtures.
    14	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/vercel` — Vercel-owned Schemas, identities,
    15	  services, safe errors, and explicit read/write-capability Layers. Preview
    16	  configuration and stable-environment authority loaders expose only their
    17	  owner-named authority error and bounded reason Schema; raw Config,
    18	  filesystem, parser, and primitive-string failures remain private.
    19	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/photon` — retained Photon observation Resources and
    20	  the separately composed Preview webhook-binding capability.
    21	
    22	Raw provider clients, wire DTOs, credentials, secret values, and unchecked
    23	provider failures are not public exports.
    24	
    25	Infrastructure operator programs keep owner-local Schema tagged errors until
    26	their final process adapter. That adapter alone may render the stable bounded
    27	status/reason and set the documented exit code. Root lint rejects primitive
    28	`Effect.fail`, `Effect.failSync`, and `Effect.mapError` values across every
    29	script in `scripts/`. Reusable live Layers retain typed construction failures;
    30	commands provide their runtime inside the final catch/exit boundary, and root
    31	lint rejects `Layer.orDie` in package source and infrastructure scripts.
    32	Subprocess fixtures exercise deterministic foreground stops and missing Layer
    33	configuration without provider transport or raw Cause output. Mutating
    34	commands capture authority, configuration, runtime acquisition, foreground
    35	work, readback, and Schema receipt encoding in that boundary; expected failure
    36	must not fall through to a runtime stack reporter. The private automatic
    37	Production entrypoint follows the same process contract: it keeps the existing
    38	Schema-encoded deployment receipt on success and emits only
    39	`{"status":"blocked"}` with exit code `1` after any Config, Layer, deployment,
    40	rollback, health, or encoding failure. That bounded result is not a deployment
    41	or rollback diagnosis; GitHub logs and Vercel readback remain the operational
    42	evidence owners.
    43	
    44	## Supported commands
    45	
    46	Run package checks from the repository root:
    47	
    48	```sh
    49	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure check-types
    50	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure test
    51	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure build
    52	```
    53	
    54	Public repository command names are `infrastructure:inventory`,
    55	`infrastructure:adoption-manifest`, `infrastructure:adoption-proof`,
    56	`infrastructure:drift-report`, `infrastructure:preview-plan`,
    57	`infrastructure:preview-apply`, `infrastructure:preview-sync`,
    58	`infrastructure:preview-drift`, `infrastructure:preview-repair`,
    59	`infrastructure:preview-rollback-plan`, `infrastructure:preview-rollback`,
    60	`infrastructure:preview-state-migration`,
    61	`infrastructure:production-state-migration`,
    62	`infrastructure:stable-preview-plan`,
    63	`infrastructure:stable-preview-apply`,
    64	`infrastructure:stable-preview-sync`,
    65	`infrastructure:stable-production-plan`,
    66	`infrastructure:stable-production-apply`,
    67	`infrastructure:stable-production-sync`,
    68	`infrastructure:photon-candidate-inventory`,
    69	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-register`,
    70	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-binding`,
    71	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-register`,
    72	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-delete`, and
    73	`infrastructure:vercel-git-link-authority`. `production:deploy` is the private
    74	post-CI Production entrypoint. It is owned by the exact-SHA `Production`
    75	workflow, uses two separately revocable Vercel credentials project-scoped to
    76	the exact Personal projects and selected by exact project binding, proves the
    77	assigned-project read and sibling-project denial before custody, and stages both apps with
    78	domains skipped, validates immutable candidates, promotes only while the
    79	candidate is still `main`, verifies the stable targets and proxy health, and
    80	restores the exact prior deployments on every non-success Effect exit after
    81	promotion starts, including interruption and defect paths. It is not an
    82	operator convenience command.
    83	
    84	`infrastructure:drift-report` uses a distinct project-scoped credential Layer.
    85	Its environment file supplies
    86	`BUNDJIL_INFRASTRUCTURE_VERCEL_PROJECT_CREDENTIALS_JSON`, a Schema-decoded
    87	non-empty array of unique project-ID/token bindings. Each token is issued for
    88	one exact Personal Vercel project and must pass the assigned-project read and
    89	sibling-project denial checks before custody. The Vercel adapter selects a
    90	redacted token only after receiving a decoded branded project ID, and the
    91	Alchemy project provider observes exactly the manifest projects rather than
    92	listing a whole team. Broad `VERCEL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ACCESS_TOKEN` custody remains
    93	limited to the separate inventory/adoption/operator paths.
    94	
    95	Marketplace attachment reads use only each exact project's decoded
    96	environment `contentHint`. Project tokens cannot enumerate the account-wide
    97	storage list, so the adapter never calls it. The accepted manifest database ID
    98	is retained only after the observable integration, configuration, resource and
    99	project identities match; it is not a fresh database-ID readback.
   100	
   101	The accepted Preview manifest is Schema-encoded first, then held in the exact
   102	GitHub manifest secret as an in-memory gzip/base64 transport because the raw
   103	155-resource JSON exceeds GitHub's secret-size boundary. The hosted workflow
   104	materialises the original JSON into mode-`0600` custody before this command
   105	Schema-decodes it and compares it with the exact configured accepted digest;
   106	the transport is never a second manifest authority.
   107	Vercel deployment responses may also contain named custom targets. The live
   108	adapter decodes those provider values but admits only `preview`, `production`,
   109	or the provider's legacy `null` Preview target into Bundjil observations;
   110	custom targets such as `staging` are ignored and are never relabelled Preview.

     1	# `@bundjil/infrastructure`
     2	
     3	Private repository infrastructure contracts and Alchemy providers for Bundjil.
     4	The package owns state-safe Schemas, branded identities, named services, safe
     5	errors, explicit live/memory Layers, adoption and inventory contracts, bounded
     6	receipts, and retained custom Resources.
     7	
     8	## Public exports
     9	
    10	- `@bundjil/infrastructure` — shared infrastructure contracts, services,
    11	  configuration, receipts, inventory, drift, state, adoption, and synthetic
    12	  provider capabilities.
    13	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/testing` — decoded deterministic test fixtures.
    14	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/vercel` — Vercel-owned Schemas, identities,
    15	  services, safe errors, and explicit read/write-capability Layers. Preview
    16	  configuration and stable-environment authority loaders expose only their
    17	  owner-named authority error and bounded reason Schema; raw Config,
    18	  filesystem, parser, and primitive-string failures remain private.
    19	- `@bundjil/infrastructure/photon` — retained Photon observation Resources and
    20	  the separately composed Preview webhook-binding capability.
    21	
    22	Raw provider clients, wire DTOs, credentials, secret values, and unchecked
    23	provider failures are not public exports.
    24	
    25	Infrastructure operator programs keep owner-local Schema tagged errors until
    26	their final process adapter. That adapter alone may render the stable bounded
    27	status/reason and set the documented exit code. Root lint rejects primitive
    28	`Effect.fail`, `Effect.failSync`, and `Effect.mapError` values across every
    29	script in `scripts/`. Reusable live Layers retain typed construction failures;
    30	commands provide their runtime inside the final catch/exit boundary, and root
    31	lint rejects `Layer.orDie` in package source and infrastructure scripts.
    32	Subprocess fixtures exercise deterministic foreground stops and missing Layer
    33	configuration without provider transport or raw Cause output. Mutating
    34	commands capture authority, configuration, runtime acquisition, foreground
    35	work, readback, and Schema receipt encoding in that boundary; expected failure
    36	must not fall through to a runtime stack reporter. The private automatic
    37	Production entrypoint follows the same process contract: it keeps the existing
    38	Schema-encoded deployment receipt on success and emits only
    39	`{"status":"blocked"}` with exit code `1` after any Config, Layer, deployment,
    40	rollback, health, or encoding failure. That bounded result is not a deployment
    41	or rollback diagnosis; GitHub logs and Vercel readback remain the operational
    42	evidence owners.
    43	
    44	## Supported commands
    45	
    46	Run package checks from the repository root:
    47	
    48	```sh
    49	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure check-types
    50	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure test
    51	bun run --filter=@bundjil/infrastructure build
    52	```
    53	
    54	Public repository command names are `infrastructure:inventory`,
    55	`infrastructure:adoption-manifest`, `infrastructure:adoption-proof`,
    56	`infrastructure:drift-report`, `infrastructure:preview-plan`,
    57	`infrastructure:preview-apply`, `infrastructure:preview-sync`,
    58	`infrastructure:preview-drift`, `infrastructure:preview-repair`,
    59	`infrastructure:preview-rollback-plan`, `infrastructure:preview-rollback`,
    60	`infrastructure:preview-state-migration`,
    61	`infrastructure:production-state-migration`,
    62	`infrastructure:stable-preview-plan`,
    63	`infrastructure:stable-preview-apply`,
    64	`infrastructure:stable-preview-sync`,
    65	`infrastructure:stable-production-plan`,
    66	`infrastructure:stable-production-apply`,
    67	`infrastructure:stable-production-sync`,
    68	`infrastructure:photon-candidate-inventory`,
    69	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-register`,
    70	`infrastructure:photon-preview-webhook-binding`,
    71	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-register`,
    72	`infrastructure:photon-production-webhook-delete`, and
    73	`infrastructure:vercel-git-link-authority`. `production:deploy` is the private
    74	post-CI Production entrypoint. It is owned by the exact-SHA `Production`
    75	workflow, uses two separately revocable Vercel credentials project-scoped to
    76	the exact Personal projects and selected by exact project binding, proves the
    77	assigned-project read and sibling-project denial before custody, and stages both apps with
    78	domains skipped, validates immutable candidates, promotes only while the
    79	candidate is still `main`, verifies the stable targets and proxy health, and
    80	restores the exact prior deployments on every non-success Effect exit after
    81	promotion starts, including interruption and defect paths. It is not an
    82	operator convenience command.
    83	
    84	`infrastructure:drift-report` uses a distinct project-scoped credential Layer.
    85	Its environment file supplies
    86	`BUNDJIL_INFRASTRUCTURE_VERCEL_PROJECT_CREDENTIALS_JSON`, a Schema-decoded
    87	non-empty array of unique project-ID/token bindings. Each token is issued for
    88	one exact Personal Vercel project and must pass the assigned-project read and
    89	sibling-project denial checks before custody. The Vercel adapter selects a
    90	redacted token only after receiving a decoded branded project ID, and the
    91	Alchemy project provider observes exactly the manifest projects rather than
    92	listing a whole team. Broad `VERCEL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ACCESS_TOKEN` custody remains
    93	limited to the separate inventory/adoption/operator paths.
    94	
    95	Marketplace attachment reads use only each exact project's decoded
    96	environment `contentHint`. Project tokens cannot enumerate the account-wide
    97	storage list, so the adapter never calls it. The accepted manifest database ID
    98	is retained only after the observable integration, configuration, resource and
    99	project identities match; it is not a fresh database-ID readback.
   100	
   101	The accepted Preview manifest is Schema-encoded first, then held in the exact
   102	GitHub manifest secret as an in-memory gzip/base64 transport because the raw
   103	155-resource JSON exceeds GitHub's secret-size boundary. The hosted workflow
   104	materialises the original JSON into mode-`0600` custody before this command
   105	Schema-decodes it and compares it with the exact configured accepted digest;
   106	the transport is never a second manifest authority.
   107	Vercel deployment responses may also contain named custom targets. The live
   108	adapter decodes those provider values but admits only `preview`, `production`,
   109	or the provider's legacy `null` Preview target into Bundjil observations;
   110	custom targets such as `staging` are ignored and are never relabelled Preview.
   111	The drift report keeps returned deployment observations strict across every
   112	typed field. If Vercel no longer returns an accepted historical deployment,
   113	the report records unavailable history without claiming drift, deletion,
   114	retention or repair authority. An accepted write-only environment baseline is
   115	continuous only when present provider revision metadata is unchanged and the
   116	accepted manifest records `ObservedUnknown`; the value itself is never proved.
   117	If native sync cannot complete, the operator log may expose only the closed
   118	typed provider-read error name and reason alongside the safe phase. It never
   119	emits the error message, request, response, URL, headers, provider payload or
   120	credential.
   121	
   122	## Claim boundary
   123	
   124	Package checks prove repository contracts only. They do not establish current
   125	provider state or authorize credentials, state migration, provider writes,
   126	deployment, promotion, messaging, billing, Preview, or Production operations.
   127	Current evidence belongs to task-scoped receipts and external readback.
   128	The automatic command's local tests prove orchestration and fail-closed
   129	behavior only; a successful hosted `Production` run plus Vercel readback is
   130	required to prove automatic deployment.
   131	
   132	Operational preconditions, authority, sequencing, evidence, rollback, stop,
   133	and escalation rules are owned by the
   134	[Alchemy infrastructure runbook](../../apps/agent/runbooks/alchemy-infrastructure.md).

   150	## Admin bootstrap and custody
   151	
   152	Only Cooper may initiate a bootstrap request. The request must name the target
   153	Environment, credential purpose, least-privilege provider permission groups,
   154	resource scope, allowed workflow/job, expiry or rotation trigger, approval,
   155	receipt route, rollback candidate, and escalation contact. Do not put a value,
   156	account identifier, token test, or provider response in a repository file,
   157	terminal transcript, or receipt.
   158	
   159	HGI-112 must first read back the intended GitHub Environment protection and
   160	environment-scoped secret names, then apply only the approved delta and record
   161	before/after redacted receipts. The repository's current GitHub billing plan
   162	does not support Environment required reviewers or wait timers. The fixed
   163	`site-proof` boundary therefore uses a custom `main`-only deployment branch
   164	policy plus authenticated manual dispatch by `crcorbett` and the workflow's
   165	exact ref, candidate, accepted-quality, task, operation, and plan-digest guards.
   166	This is weaker than a GitHub-required reviewer and must remain explicit in the
   167	receipt. Repository YAML and `stacks/github.ts` are not proof that those
   168	settings exist. The historical bootstrap stack is a capability only and must
   169	not be run under this task.
   170	
   171	Each protected GitHub Environment owns one secret name: `DOPPLER_TOKEN`.
   172	`preview` is a read-only service token for `site/stg_preview`, `site-proof` for
   173	`site/stg`, and `production` for `site/prd`. The Preview config contains no
   174	Axiom value. The pinned Doppler fetch action uses outputs rather than broad
   175	environment injection, so each command step still names the exact provider
   176	values it receives. The reusable callers pass no provider secret and must never
   177	use broad inheritance.
   178	
   179	The service tokens expire after one year and must be rotated before expiry.
   180	Revoke only the affected config token during rollback or an incident. Provider
   181	tokens remain in Doppler; GitHub stores no provider value for this workflow
   182	path. The sanitized hosted plan remains the first capability check and must
   183	stop on an unavailable or under-scoped value.
   184	
   185	Any new or replacement value must still pass through a secret-negative
   186	custodian path and retain names/timestamps only. If a provider Copy control
   187	cannot reach the destination secret input without exposing the value, revoke
   188	only the newly created credential, prove the recovery identity, and stop before
   189	dispatch. Do not substitute an assistant-readable clipboard, shell argument,
   190	file, workflow output, or evidence body.
   191	
   192	## Rotation, revocation, and incident stop
   193	
   194	On suspected compromise, immediately stop the affected workflow path and
   195	record the credential name, purpose, Environment, last known consumer, exact
   196	candidate/run if known, incident owner, and time. Do not print, validate,
   197	copy, rotate, revoke, or probe a value locally outside an exact task/runbook
   198	authority and secret-negative custodian boundary.
   199	
   200	Cooper escalates the external revocation and replacement request to HGI-112's
   201	approved custodian path. Keep dependent production or preview work blocked
   202	until external revocation/replacement and GitHub Environment readbacks are
   203	recorded, then use a new or reverted `main` candidate for production. The
   204	normal exact PR-lifecycle cleanup may run only through its admitted event and
   205	workflow; broader orphan, incident, account-wide, or manually selected-stage
   206	cleanup remains report-only without separate authority. This document claims
   207	no hosted revocation, replacement, deployment, cleanup, or provider recovery.
   210	
   211	The workflow definition is loaded from the current trusted default branch, and
   212	the job checks out that definition's exact `job.workflow_sha`, never PR source
   213	or a moving branch ref. Its secretless preflight reads the live PR with `github.token` and
   214	rejects another repository, author, base, state, event, label, or stale
   215	re-addition. The `preview` Environment supplies only its config-bound
   216	`DOPPLER_TOKEN`; the pinned fetch action maps `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and
   217	`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` only to the cleanup command step. It receives only the
   218	event PR number; `@packages/scripts`
   219	Schema-decodes a positive integer, derives and decodes `pr-{number}`, then runs:
   220	
   221	```bash
   222	bun alchemy destroy --stage pr-{number} --yes
   223	```
   224	
   225	After the frozen install, the workflow first runs
   226	`bun turbo run build --filter=@packages/route-verification...`. The cleanup
   227	service imports that package through its published workspace export, so this
   228	build is required on a clean runner before any Alchemy or Cloudflare command.
   229	
   230	The workflow contains no user-supplied stage, `--stage` construction, fork
   231	credential path, Axiom credential, fixed-stage selector, or Production
   232	resource. Its one manual retry supplies only the separately checked task, PR
   233	number, and head SHA. The non-production Alchemy branch owns only `Website`.
   234	An already-absent exact stage is converged when Alchemy returns success. The
   235	package then reads the exact managed PR comment. For an identified preview it
   236	reads every paginated comment and accepts exactly one marker authored by
   237	`github-actions[bot]` whose derived stage and exact live head match. It then
   238	decodes the former `workers.dev` URL and Worker name, and requires both the
   239	direct Cloudflare script read and non-redirected former public URL to return

   241	Alchemy no-change result with no managed comment is a narrower no-op and does
   242	not claim provider/public absence. A deletion without a comment, wrong author,
   243	duplicate marker, stale stage/head, another host, redirect, still-present
   244	Worker or URL, or unavailable readback remains failed and
   245	retains its bounded transcript. Repeating cleanup targets the same derived
   246	stage and no other resource.
   247	
   248	After the cleanup command starts, the workflow uploads its machine receipt and
   249	sanitized detail artifact for 30 days before propagating command failure. A
   250	preflight failure may create no command file; in that case the GitHub job log
   251	and a bounded repository stop receipt retain the failure and the explicit
   252	pre-provider non-claim. A successful receipt binds the
   253	exact event-derived stage to either an explicit unidentified Alchemy no-op or
   254	the Alchemy destroy result, managed-comment Worker identity, direct Cloudflare
   255	`404`, and former public URL `404`. The
   256	hosted event, trusted workflow SHA and job identity still belong in the final
   257	repository receipt. Missing identity or unavailable readback is inconclusive,
   258	not absence.

   260	Recovery for an open PR is to re-add `deploy-preview` and let a new exact-head
   261	quality/deploy cycle recreate the stage. Run `32311147280` proved that PR #90's

   275	```

   278	deleted one `Website` from `pr-90`, uploaded artifact `9390510444`, bound the
   279	managed GitHub Actions comment to the exact Worker, and recorded direct

   283	owns the exact identities, `94/100` minute accounting and limits. Do not repeat

   286	A closed PR cannot be redeployed; open a new PR. Never recover by re-adding the

   317	## Sequential privileged-preview procedure
   318	
   319	1. Record the accepted task, trusted maintainer identity, exact reviewed SHA,
   320	   fixed `site-proof` stage, intended operation, credential lifetime and
   321	   revocation path, receipt path, rollback/cleanup target, and escalation.

   324	   rejects arbitrary stages, missing quality/proof, unadmitted task classes,
   325	   non-main candidates, and secrets outside the privileged job, then confirm
   326	   the current HGI-112 setting receipt matches that contract.

   328	   `site-proof`; stop on unavailable readback, another stage, an unaccounted

   145	
   146	### CI-unavailable temporary runner fallback
   147	
   148	When GitHub refuses to start `ubuntu-latest` jobs because hosted Actions usage
   149	or billing is unavailable, do not treat the skipped job as quality, Preview,
   150	site-proof, or Production evidence. An explicitly approved exact-main
   151	candidate may instead dispatch `ci.yml` with `runner_label` set to a dedicated
   152	temporary self-hosted repository-runner label and `force_apply=true`. The
   153	legacy force input selects the existing main-only manual path; it does not
   154	bypass the Axiom capacity preflight, accepted plan digest, protected
   155	`site-proof` and `production` Environments, fixed-stage ordering, or provider
   156	readbacks.
   157	
   158	Register the runner only for the approved repository and exact workflow run,
   159	using a fresh one-use registration token. Before dispatch, read back Actions
   160	Runner `2.327.1` or newer: the exact pinned `actions/cache@v6.1.0` used by
   161	quality declares the Node 24 action runtime. Keep the dedicated label
   162	unavailable to every other workflow dispatch, then stop the process and remove
   163	the runner with a fresh removal token immediately after the terminal workflow result.
   164	Never route pull-request work or an untrusted ref to this runner. Retain the
   165	runner's non-secret name, labels, registration/removal timestamps, exact
   166	candidate and run IDs, and the same sanitized artifacts required by the hosted
   167	path. If any protected secret or Environment is unavailable to the self-hosted
   168	job, stop; do not copy secret values into the local shell or workflow inputs.
   169	
   170	## Missing-approval procedure
   171	
   172	1. Record the candidate commit and requested environment.
   173	2. Confirm that required local checks and the candidate graph are present in
   174	   source; do not execute a hosted workflow or provider command.
   175	3. Produce a `blocked-by-SITE-D1` receipt with the missing exact SHA/run or
   176	   Environment approval and
   177	   the default recovery target: a new or reverted main-branch candidate.
   178	4. Escalate to Cooper; do not invoke a hosted workflow or provider command.

145	All action references use immutable full commit SHAs. The Site
   146	infrastructure/security maintainer owns review and replacement of those pins;
   147	each update needs an upstream provenance check, static contract pass, and a
   148	new candidate rather than an in-place hosted change.
   149	
   150	## Admin bootstrap and custody
   151	
   152	Only Cooper may initiate a bootstrap request. The request must name the target
   153	Environment, credential purpose, least-privilege provider permission groups,
   154	resource scope, allowed workflow/job, expiry or rotation trigger, approval,
   155	receipt route, rollback candidate, and escalation contact. Do not put a value,
   156	account identifier, token test, or provider response in a repository file,
   157	terminal transcript, or receipt.
   158	
   159	HGI-112 must first read back the intended GitHub Environment protection and
   160	environment-scoped secret names, then apply only the approved delta and record
   161	before/after redacted receipts. The repository's current GitHub billing plan
   162	does not support Environment required reviewers or wait timers. The fixed
   163	`site-proof` boundary therefore uses a custom `main`-only deployment branch
   164	policy plus authenticated manual dispatch by `crcorbett` and the workflow's
   165	exact ref, candidate, accepted-quality, task, operation, and plan-digest guards.
   166	This is weaker than a GitHub-required reviewer and must remain explicit in the
   167	receipt. Repository YAML and `stacks/github.ts` are not proof that those
   168	settings exist. The historical bootstrap stack is a capability only and must
   169	not be run under this task.
   170	
   171	Each protected GitHub Environment owns one secret name: `DOPPLER_TOKEN`.
   172	`preview` is a read-only service token for `site/stg_preview`, `site-proof` for
   173	`site/stg`, and `production` for `site/prd`. The Preview config contains no
   174	Axiom value. The pinned Doppler fetch action uses outputs rather than broad
   175	environment injection, so each command step still names the exact provider
   176	values it receives. The reusable callers pass no provider secret and must never
   177	use broad inheritance.
   178	
   179	The service tokens expire after one year and must be rotated before expiry.
   180	Revoke only the affected config token during rollback or an incident. Provider
   181	tokens remain in Doppler; GitHub stores no provider value for this workflow
   182	path. The sanitized hosted plan remains the first capability check and must
   183	stop on an unavailable or under-scoped value.
   184	
   185	Any new or replacement value must still pass through a secret-negative
   186	custodian path and retain names/timestamps only. If a provider Copy control
   187	cannot reach the destination secret input without exposing the value, revoke
   188	only the newly created credential, prove the recovery identity, and stop before
   189	dispatch. Do not substitute an assistant-readable clipboard, shell argument,
   190	file, workflow output, or evidence body.
   191	
   192	## Rotation, revocation, and incident stop
   193	
   194	On suspected compromise, immediately stop the affected workflow path and
   195	record the credential name, purpose, Environment, last known consumer, exact
   196	candidate/run if known, incident owner, and time. Do not print, validate,
   197	copy, rotate, revoke, or probe a value locally outside an exact task/runbook
   198	authority and secret-negative custodian boundary.
   199	
   200	Cooper escalates the external revocation and replacement request to HGI-112's
   201	approved custodian path. Keep dependent production or preview work blocked
   202	until external revocation/replacement and GitHub Environment readbacks are
   203	recorded, then use a new or reverted `main` candidate for production. The
   204	normal exact PR-lifecycle cleanup may run only through its admitted event and
   205	workflow; broader orphan, incident, account-wide, or manually selected-stage
   206	cleanup remains report-only without separate authority. This document claims
   207	no hosted revocation, replacement, deployment, cleanup, or provider recovery.
   210	
   211	The workflow definition is loaded from the current trusted default branch, and
   212	the job checks out that definition's exact `job.workflow_sha`, never PR source
   213	or a moving branch ref. Its secretless preflight reads the live PR with `github.token` and
   214	rejects another repository, author, base, state, event, label, or stale
   215	re-addition. The `preview` Environment supplies only its config-bound
   216	`DOPPLER_TOKEN`; the pinned fetch action maps `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and
   217	`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` only to the cleanup command step. It receives only the
   218	event PR number; `@packages/scripts`
   219	Schema-decodes a positive integer, derives and decodes `pr-{number}`, then runs:
   220	
   221	```bash
   222	bun alchemy destroy --stage pr-{number} --yes
   223	```
   224	
   225	After the frozen install, the workflow first runs
   226	`bun turbo run build --filter=@packages/route-verification...`. The cleanup
   227	service imports that package through its published workspace export, so this
   228	build is required on a clean runner before any Alchemy or Cloudflare command.
   229	
   230	The workflow contains no user-supplied stage, `--stage` construction, fork
   231	credential path, Axiom credential, fixed-stage selector, or Production
   232	resource. Its one manual retry supplies only the separately checked task, PR
   233	number, and head SHA. The non-production Alchemy branch owns only `Website`.
   234	An already-absent exact stage is converged when Alchemy returns success. The
   235	package then reads the exact managed PR comment. For an identified preview it
   236	reads every paginated comment and accepts exactly one marker authored by
   237	`github-actions[bot]` whose derived stage and exact live head match. It then
   238	decodes the former `workers.dev` URL and Worker name, and requires both the
   239	direct Cloudflare script read and non-redirected former public URL to return
   240	`404`. An exact
   241	Alchemy no-change result with no managed comment is a narrower no-op and does
   242	not claim provider/public absence. A deletion without a comment, wrong author,
   243	duplicate marker, stale stage/head, another host, redirect, still-present
   244	Worker or URL, or unavailable readback remains failed and
   245	retains its bounded transcript. Repeating cleanup targets the same derived
   246	stage and no other resource.
   247	
   248	After the cleanup command starts, the workflow uploads its machine receipt and
   249	sanitized detail artifact for 30 days before propagating command failure. A
   250	preflight failure may create no command file; in that case the GitHub job log
   251	and a bounded repository stop receipt retain the failure and the explicit
   252	pre-provider non-claim. A successful receipt binds the
   253	exact event-derived stage to either an explicit unidentified Alchemy no-op or
   254	the Alchemy destroy result, managed-comment Worker identity, direct Cloudflare
   255	`404`, and former public URL `404`. The
   256	hosted event, trusted workflow SHA and job identity still belong in the final
   257	repository receipt. Missing identity or unavailable readback is inconclusive,
   258	not absence.
   259	
   260	Recovery for an open PR is to re-add `deploy-preview` and let a new exact-head
   261	quality/deploy cycle recreate the stage. Run `32311147280` proved that PR #90's
   262	close event stopped before provider access because its trusted revision lacked
   263	the clean-checkout route-verification build. Approved label removal then
   264	triggered run `32320904569`, but GitHub's `pull_request` event reused that older
   265	revision and its open-state check stopped before Bun or credentials. For this
   266	already closed PR, skip-CI PR #100 delivered the `pull_request_target`
   267	correction as main `80b45e9a`, then the approved operator invoked exactly:
   268	
   269	```bash
   270	gh workflow run cloudflare-branch-preview-cleanup.yml \
   271	  --ref main \
   272	  -f accepted_task=CIE-005 \
   273	  -f pr_number=90 \
   274	  -f head_sha=189613845cad1b72fda78eb33fde3cf9146ff68e
   275	```
   276	
   277	Run `32323359738` succeeded in 53 seconds. It accepted the exact live PR/head,
   278	deleted one `Website` from `pr-90`, uploaded artifact `9390510444`, bound the
   279	managed GitHub Actions comment to the exact Worker, and recorded direct
   280	Cloudflare-script plus non-redirected former-URL `404` readbacks. An independent
   281	direct public request later returned `404`. The retained
   282	[`CIE-005-cleanup-success-20260820.json`](../../verification/artifacts/CIE-005-cleanup-success-20260820.json)
   283	owns the exact identities, `94/100` minute accounting and limits. Do not repeat
   284	the task-bound dispatch; future cleanup uses only a new admitted PR lifecycle.
   285	
   286	A closed PR cannot be redeployed; open a new PR. Never recover by re-adding the
   287	label to PR #90, supplying an arbitrary stage, canceling an active mutation,
   288	broadening the preview token, or targeting `site-proof`/`prod`.
   289	
   290	The Axiom-only `proof` job admits `AOX-*` or exact `SAD-004` only. For any other
   291	task or operation, retain a `workflow-task-not-admitted` receipt and stop
   292	before dispatch or provider mutation. Exact `MCP-005` additionally requires a merged
   293	current-main candidate and fresh readback that AOX-006 has released the fixed
   294	stage. The readback must be committed as
   295	`docs/verification/artifacts/MCP-005-site-proof-stage-release-readback.json`;
   296	a secretless job without the `site-proof` Environment receives its exact
   297	SHA-256, Schema-decodes the file, and emits the sole output that can admit
   298	credentialed plan/deploy. The package runtime rejects byte drift again before
   299	a provider command. All site-proof workflow runs share one stage-wide
   300	concurrency group. A branch push, completed GitHub job, or existing `site-proof`
   301	Worker is not sufficient.
   302	
   303	PR #14 has one narrow source-promotion exception because GitHub rejected both
   304	of its hosted jobs before checkout with zero steps and the same account
   305	billing/spending-limit annotation. Record those failures as `ci-unavailable`,
   306	never as passing CI, and do not dispatch or retry another Actions run. This
   307	exception applies only to PR #14 and its mechanical post-AOX reconciliation.
   308	It does not change an evergreen workflow, policy, or required check. After
   309	fresh AOX release readback, the final exact-main candidate must repeat the
   310	complete local repository, MCP protocol/parity/workflow, emitted
   311	Worker/workerd, documentation/skills, and independent-review gates. Only then
   312	may an operator use the minimum required-check override, read back the merged
   313	commit and tree, and continue to the secretless MCP stage-release preflight.
   314	The bounded receipt is
   315	[`MCP-005-pr14-ci-unavailable-local-substitute-readback.json`](../../verification/artifacts/MCP-005-pr14-ci-unavailable-local-substitute-readback.json).
   316	
   317	## Sequential privileged-preview procedure
   318	
   319	1. Record the accepted task, trusted maintainer identity, exact reviewed SHA,
   320	   fixed `site-proof` stage, intended operation, credential lifetime and
   321	   revocation path, receipt path, rollback/cleanup target, and escalation.
   322	2. Confirm HGI-105's workflow contract still excludes forks and ordinary pull
   323	   requests from provider credentials. Confirm HGI-107's fixed-stage caller
   324	   rejects arbitrary stages, missing quality/proof, unadmitted task classes,
   325	   non-main candidates, and secrets outside the privileged job, then confirm
   326	   the current HGI-112 setting receipt matches that contract.
   327	3. Run [inventory and preflight](inventory-and-preflight.md) for exactly
   328	   `site-proof`; stop on unavailable readback, another stage, an unaccounted
   329	   open-task dependency, or any mismatch.
   330	4. For `MCP-005`, confirm AOX-006 has first completed or explicitly released
   145	
   146	### CI-unavailable temporary runner fallback
   147	
   148	When GitHub refuses to start `ubuntu-latest` jobs because hosted Actions usage
   149	or billing is unavailable, do not treat the skipped job as quality, Preview,
   150	site-proof, or Production evidence. An explicitly approved exact-main
   151	candidate may instead dispatch `ci.yml` with `runner_label` set to a dedicated
   152	temporary self-hosted repository-runner label and `force_apply=true`. The
   153	legacy force input selects the existing main-only manual path; it does not
   154	bypass the Axiom capacity preflight, accepted plan digest, protected
   155	`site-proof` and `production` Environments, fixed-stage ordering, or provider
   156	readbacks.
   157	
   158	Register the runner only for the approved repository and exact workflow run,
   159	using a fresh one-use registration token. Before dispatch, read back Actions
   160	Runner `2.327.1` or newer: the exact pinned `actions/cache@v6.1.0` used by
   161	quality declares the Node 24 action runtime. Keep the dedicated label
   162	unavailable to every other workflow dispatch, then stop the process and remove
   163	the runner with a fresh removal token immediately after the terminal workflow result.
   164	Never route pull-request work or an untrusted ref to this runner. Retain the
   165	runner's non-secret name, labels, registration/removal timestamps, exact
   166	candidate and run IDs, and the same sanitized artifacts required by the hosted
   167	path. If any protected secret or Environment is unavailable to the self-hosted
   168	job, stop; do not copy secret values into the local shell or workflow inputs.
   169	
   170	## Missing-approval procedure
   171	
   172	1. Record the candidate commit and requested environment.
   173	2. Confirm that required local checks and the candidate graph are present in
   174	   source; do not execute a hosted workflow or provider command.
   175	3. Produce a `blocked-by-SITE-D1` receipt with the missing exact SHA/run or
   176	   Environment approval and
   177	   the default recovery target: a new or reverted main-branch candidate.
   178	4. Escalate to Cooper; do not invoke a hosted workflow or provider command.
   179	
   180	## MCP-006 Production completion (2026-08-06)
