     2	
     3	The root `alchemy.run.ts` is one Effect composition root. It owns a staged
     4	`Cloudflare.Worker`, one OAuth KV namespace and the Worker's bindings. The
     5	production stage also owns the Google login method used by Cloudflare Access.
     6	The Worker uses Cloudflare's stateless MCP handler; no Durable Object is needed.
     7	The `prd` stage owns the Worker custom-domain attachment for
     8	`instapaper.coopercorbett.com`. The existing `coopercorbett.com` zone remains
     9	foreign infrastructure. Production disables the `workers.dev` surface, while
    10	non-production stages retain their stage-specific `workers.dev` address.
    11	
    12	Secret Worker bindings are `Config.redacted` inputs resolved only by the
    13	deployment process. The Google client secret is supplied by Doppler directly to
    14	Alchemy's Access identity-provider resource. Alchemy's remote state is encrypted
    15	at rest; repository files, command output and proof records must not contain the
    16	clear secret.
    17	
    18	Google is the human login provider for Cloudflare Access. The Google Cloud
    19	project and its OAuth client are external prerequisites because this repository
    20	does not manage Google Cloud. The existing Access SaaS application and its
    21	exact-email policy also remain foreign. Alchemy owns only the account-level
    22	Google login method because the selected Alchemy version cannot safely describe
    23	every setting on the existing SaaS application. After an Alchemy apply, a
    24	bounded Cloudflare API update may attach the owned login method to that existing
    25	application. It must preserve the application's client, redirect and policy
    26	settings.
    27	
    28	The shared Access OIDC application registers separate development and
    29	production Worker callback URLs. Each Alchemy stage still has its own Worker,
    30	OAuth KV namespace and cookie-encryption key. Access admits only the configured
    31	allowed email, and the Worker independently checks the same email in the

    35	`/privacy`. The external Google project registers those pages under the
    36	authorised domain and has publishing status `In production`. The app requests
    37	only basic Google sign-in identity; its Data Access page lists no sensitive or
    38	restricted scopes. Google's broader audience setting does not replace the

    43	apply, fail on unexpected deletes and read the Worker and KV namespace back

     4

     6	secret-store project/config, Worker name, OAuth KV namespace and rollback
     7	target in a private operator record, not in this repository.

    12

    14	Register the Worker's `/callback` URL, enable PKCE, request the
    15	`openid email profile` scopes, and keep an allow policy for Cooper. Copy the
    16	exact issuer, authorization, token and JWKS URLs into the matching secret names.
    17	`MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_HOSTNAMES` is a comma-separated list of hostnames, not full
    18	URLs.

    21	web client must register the Cloudflare Access team origin and callback supplied

    26	`https://instapaper.coopercorbett.com/privacy`. Register `coopercorbett.com` as

    29	sensitive or restricted scopes. Do not add a logo unless brand verification is

    35	`GOOGLE_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` in the approved production secret-store
    36	configuration. Do not put either value or the private configuration name in a

    38

    42

     2	
     3	The root `alchemy.run.ts` is one Effect composition root. It owns a staged
     4	`Cloudflare.Worker`, one OAuth KV namespace and the Worker's bindings. The
     5	production stage also owns the Google login method used by Cloudflare Access.
     6	The Worker uses Cloudflare's stateless MCP handler; no Durable Object is needed.
     7	The `prd` stage owns the Worker custom-domain attachment for
     8	`instapaper.coopercorbett.com`. The existing `coopercorbett.com` zone remains
     9	foreign infrastructure. Production disables the `workers.dev` surface, while
    10	non-production stages retain their stage-specific `workers.dev` address.
    11	
    12	Secret Worker bindings are `Config.redacted` inputs resolved only by the
    13	deployment process. The Google client secret is supplied by Doppler directly to
    14	Alchemy's Access identity-provider resource. Alchemy's remote state is encrypted
    15	at rest; repository files, command output and proof records must not contain the
    16	clear secret.
    17	
    18	Google is the human login provider for Cloudflare Access. The Google Cloud
    19	project and its OAuth client are external prerequisites because this repository
    20	does not manage Google Cloud. The existing Access SaaS application and its
    21	exact-email policy also remain foreign. Alchemy owns only the account-level
    22	Google login method because the selected Alchemy version cannot safely describe
    23	every setting on the existing SaaS application. After an Alchemy apply, a
    24	bounded Cloudflare API update may attach the owned login method to that existing
    25	application. It must preserve the application's client, redirect and policy
    26	settings.
    27	
    28	The shared Access OIDC application registers separate development and
    29	production Worker callback URLs. Each Alchemy stage still has its own Worker,
    30	OAuth KV namespace and cookie-encryption key. Access admits only the configured
    31	allowed email, and the Worker independently checks the same email in the
    32	verified ID token before it grants MCP access.
    33

    35	`/privacy`. The external Google project registers those pages under the
    36	authorised domain and has publishing status `In production`. The app requests
    37	only basic Google sign-in identity; its Data Access page lists no sensitive or
    38	restricted scopes. Google's broader audience setting does not replace the
    39	exact-email checks in Access and the Worker.
    40	
    41	Alchemy remote state and Cloudflare provider state remain authoritative for
    42	live identity. Follow `docs/runbooks/deploy-instapaper-mcp.md`: plan before
    43	apply, fail on unexpected deletes and read the Worker and KV namespace back
    44	before making a deployment claim. The selected Alchemy beta is recorded in
    45	`repo-structure.render.json`; upgrades open a new compatibility check.
     1	# Plan, deploy and read back the Instapaper MCP
     2	
     3	## Preconditions and authority
     4	
     5	Record the operator identity, Alchemy profile, Cloudflare account, exact stage,
     6	secret-store project/config, Worker name, OAuth KV namespace and rollback
     7	target in a private operator record, not in this repository.
     8	Confirm that Cooper has approved the stage and that the Cloudflare token can
     9	manage Workers, KV, Worker secrets and Access login methods. The Cloudflare
    10	Access SaaS application and policy must already exist. Read them before any
    11	change and confirm the policy includes only the configured allowed email.
    12	
    13	Use a generic OIDC SaaS application between the Worker and Cloudflare Access.
    14	Register the Worker's `/callback` URL, enable PKCE, request the
    15	`openid email profile` scopes, and keep an allow policy for Cooper. Copy the
    16	exact issuer, authorization, token and JWKS URLs into the matching secret names.
    17	`MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_HOSTNAMES` is a comma-separated list of hostnames, not full
    18	URLs.
    19	
    20	Use the dedicated external Google Cloud project for the Access login. Its OAuth
    21	web client must register the Cloudflare Access team origin and callback supplied
    22	by the provider. Do not record that account-specific team domain here.
    23

    25	`https://instapaper.coopercorbett.com/` and privacy notice at
    26	`https://instapaper.coopercorbett.com/privacy`. Register `coopercorbett.com` as
    27	an authorised domain, keep the approved private support and developer contacts,
    28	and confirm Google's Data Access page lists no
    29	sensitive or restricted scopes. Do not add a logo unless brand verification is
    30	separately planned. Publishing makes the Google client available to Google
    31	accounts generally; Cloudflare Access and the Worker must still enforce the
    32	exact personal email.

    35	`GOOGLE_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` in the approved production secret-store
    36	configuration. Do not put either value or the private configuration name in a
    37	command argument, repository file, log or evidence record.

    40	the Alchemy process; clear values must not appear in source, state, command
    41	arguments, logs or evidence.

    44	reveal the secret again. The current Access application is the sole identity
    45	application for this service. If either the Cloudflare or Google client pair is
    46	lost or compromised, treat that as a separately approved credential rotation:
    47	create one replacement, update the approved production secret configuration,
    48	deploy and verify the hosted
    49	OAuth journey, then remove the superseded credential. Never keep two active
    50	Instapaper Access applications after verification.
    51	
    52	Production uses the approved Alchemy stage and a private secret-store
    53	configuration. Its canonical address is
    54	`https://instapaper.coopercorbett.com/mcp`, and its Access callback is
    55	`https://instapaper.coopercorbett.com/callback`. The production
    56	cookie-encryption key must differ from development. The Access client and
    57	Instapaper OAuth 1.0a credentials may be shared deliberately because they refer
    58	to the same single-user upstream services.

    60	## Procedure and bounded evidence
    61	
    62	1. Run local verification and retain the commit SHA and clean/dirty status.
    63	2. Read the selected Alchemy profile and Cloudflare account. Stop on mismatch.
    64	3. Run `doppler run --project <project> --config <config> -- bun run infra:plan -- --stage <stage>`.

    66	   the expected plan is one account-level Google identity provider and no Worker
    67	   or KV replacement. Any delete, replacement or unrelated resource is a stop
    68	   condition. Ensure the Google client secret is absent from plan output.
    69	5. Apply the same commit, profile, Doppler config and stage with
    70	   `doppler run --project <project> --config <config> -- bun run infra:deploy -- --stage <stage>`.
    71	6. Read the Google identity provider back from Cloudflare and confirm its name,
    72	   type and client ID without retaining its secret. Read the existing Access
    73	   application and policy again before attaching the provider.
    74	7. Attach only the new Google identity-provider ID to the existing Access SaaS
    75	   application and enable direct redirect to that provider. Use the smallest
    76	   supported Cloudflare update. If the API requires the whole application,
    77	   round-trip the observed document and change only `allowed_idps` and
    78	   `auto_redirect_to_identity`. Stop if any client, redirect or policy value
    79	   would change.

    81	   allowed identity provider is the owned Google provider and the allow policy
    82	   still contains exactly the configured allowed email.
    83	9. Read Google's Branding, Audience and Data Access pages. Confirm the public
    84	   home and privacy URLs, authorised domains, `In production` status and absence
    85	   of sensitive or restricted scopes.

    87	    configured account owner, and run the read-only `instapaper_access_check`.

    89	    protocol used by Executor. Do not save a bookmark.
    90	11. Record bounded receipts only. Do not retain secret bindings, OAuth tokens,
    91	    authorisation codes, full provider payloads or article text.
    92	
    93	## Rollback, escalation, and cleanup
    94	
    95	Revoke the MCP OAuth grant or Cloudflare Access policy first if access must stop
    96	immediately. To roll back only the login change, re-enable the previously
    97	verified login method on the existing application before detaching Google. Do
    98	not delete the Alchemy-owned Google identity provider until the rollback journey
    99	passes and a destructive plan is separately approved. Restore the last

   101	also changed. If publishing itself causes a Google-side problem, return the app
   102	to Testing only after confirming the configured account owner remains a test
   103	user.
   104	Provider readback proves only the named resources and settings; it does not
   105	prove publisher extraction or a successful Instapaper save.

     2	
     3	## Preconditions and authority
     4	
     5	Cooper must approve this one-time xAuth exchange. The local process needs the
     6	Instapaper app key and account password from 1Password, plus an authenticated

    13	   Alchemy stage. Do not use Production by default.
    14	2. Use local `op run` to inject `INSTAPAPER_CONSUMER_KEY`,

    17	3. Run `bun run auth:bootstrap`.
    18	4. Accept only `INSTAPAPER_OAUTH_BOOTSTRAP_OK`. The command writes the consumer
    19	   and access-token pair to Doppler through a mode-600 temporary file, suppresses
    20	   provider output, deletes the temporary directory and never prints a secret.
    21	5. Run a later deployed `instapaper_access_check` before any save.
    22	
    23	This bootstrap is intentionally local and one-time. Scheduled Codex Work uses
    24	the deployed Worker and does not need 1Password, Doppler or this Mac.
    25	
    26	## Rollback, escalation, and cleanup
    27	
    28	If the process fails, confirm that no temporary `instapaper-oauth-*` directory
    29	remains in the system temporary folder and retry only after fixing the named
    30	precondition. If custody is uncertain, revoke the Instapaper application token,
    31	rotate the consumer secret if available, and replace the Doppler values. Token
    32	bootstrap does not prove Cloudflare deployment or create a bookmark.

    61	## CI workflow and cache ownership
    62	
    63	`.github/workflows/pull-request.yml` and `.github/workflows/main.yml` are the
    64	only CI entry points. They call the reusable quality workflow at
    65	`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which owns the six required jobs, final repository
    66	validation after the build, and the final quality summary. The pull-request
    67	entry point cancels obsolete runs for the same PR; the main entry point does
    68	not cancel a run because a newer PR starts.
    69	Vercel Preview and Production remain a separate Vercel Git claim.
    70	
    71	Every job installs Node `24` with the pinned `actions/setup-node` `v7.0.0`
    72	action before Bun and repository commands. `actions/checkout` is pinned to
    73	`v7.0.1`, whose action runtime is Node 24, and the split Bun cache uses
    74	`actions/cache` `v6.1.0`, whose restore/save action runtimes are also Node 24.
    75	The bounded quality summary artifact uses `actions/upload-artifact` `v7.0.1`,
    76	which also runs on Node 24.
    77	The Node executable is pinned separately because an action's runtime does not
    78	change the shell's Node executable; the installed Eve CLI requires Node 24.
    79	
    80	Each job installs Bun `1.3.14` with `--frozen-lockfile` and caches only Bun's
    81	global package cache. The key includes runner OS, architecture, Bun version,
    82	and the complete `bun.lock` hash. The workflow does not cache `node_modules`.
    83	
    84	Turbo hashes `BUN_VERSION` and `NODE_VERSION` as global environment inputs,
    85	alongside the two declared Pollsor agent deployment inputs. Changing either
    86	toolchain version therefore creates a new task-cache namespace rather than
    87	reusing outputs built by a different runtime.
    88	
    89	Turbo Remote Cache is the default for normal type, test, and build commands.
    90	People use the root `check-types`, `test`, `build`, and `verification` commands;
    91	each selects Doppler project `pollsor` and config `ci` explicitly before calling
    92	the matching credential-neutral `*:internal` command. GitHub uses the pinned
    93	official Doppler Secrets Fetch action and maps only its `TURBO_TEAM` and
    94	`TURBO_TOKEN` outputs into the exact internal Turbo command step. It does not
    95	call a root Doppler wrapper after fetching the same values.

   101	summaries or artifacts. The provider readback, rotation, post-merge cleanup,

   104	page.

   107	app filter. A hosted Vercel build is not a person-facing local command and must
   108	not depend on the Doppler command or receive the CI Remote Cache credentials.
   109	This also keeps a Vercel deployment separate from the GitHub CI secret path.

   116	`bun run eve:check` job exercises the credential-free agent process journey
